# The EST agent guide: make a Cyber audio plugin with your AI coding agent

<!-- Generated by node scripts/est-agent-guide.mjs from the kit's sources (for-agents.md, the validator rules, the manifest schema, the templates) and the published @cyber-est/cli 0.1.0. Do not edit: change the sources and run npm run regen. -->

**For you, the person.** Save this one file. Open your AI coding agent (one that runs commands in a terminal) in an empty folder, drag this file into it, and say what you want, for example: *"Make me a tape echo whose repeats get darker."* The agent reads the file, builds the plugin, checks it with the same checks Cyber runs, and leaves a `.est` file in `dist/`. In Cyber, on Home, open **EST PLUGINS → Add a plugin** and drop that file on it. You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 20 or newer; nothing else to install for an AssemblyScript plugin, and no account to start. No terminal? Cyber's Make your own block also has a prompt to paste into any chat assistant.

**For you, the agent.** Everything you need is in this file, top to bottom. Follow **The loop** exactly, use only the commands and functions named here, and do not stop until `est validate` says `"ok": true`. Then tell the person what you built, the choices you made, and that they should listen to it.

## What an EST plugin is

An EST plugin is a CLAP 1.2 plugin compiled to WebAssembly (wasm32, with no imports), packed with its manifest (`est.json`) into a `.est` bundle. Cyber, a browser-based audio workstation, checks a bundle when it is added, meters it (each audio block has a fuel budget), and runs it in a sandbox in an AudioWorklet. Its window, if it has one, is a web page in a sandboxed frame with no network. So a plugin:

- computes sound from its input, its parameters, its notes and the song's transport, and nothing else: no files, no clock, no network, no threads, no randomness but its own seeded generator;
- is an **effect** (audio in, audio out; a note effect is an effect with notes out) or an **instrument** (notes in, audio out);
- declares every knob as a **parameter** with a fixed numeric id, in the code and in `est.json`;
- gives the same output for the same input, bit for bit, at any sample rate.

You write it in **AssemblyScript** (TypeScript's syntax; nothing to install beyond Node: start here), **Rust** or **C/C++**. The kit (`est`, the npm package `@cyber-est/cli`) makes the folder, builds, packs, validates, tests and plays it.

## Setup

Check Node first (20 or newer):

```sh
node --version
npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 --version
```

The second line must print `0.1.0`. Always write the kit's version exactly as here: `@cyber-est/cli@0.1.0`. **Never run a bare `npx est` in a folder where the kit is not installed:** npm would fetch an unrelated package called `est`. Inside the plugin folder, once the kit is installed there (step 2 below), `npx est <command>` is the kit.

If `npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 doctor` reports something missing (Rust and C++ need their own toolchains), it prints the command that installs it.

## The loop

Make the folder, install the kit in it, then build, check and fix until it passes. For an **effect**:

<!-- guide:run effect -->
```sh
npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 new effect-as my-plugin
cd my-plugin
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0
npx est validate
npx est test
```

For an **instrument** (it plays notes):

<!-- guide:run instrument -->
```sh
npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 new instrument-as my-plugin
cd my-plugin
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0
npx est validate
npx est test
```

With **a window of its own** (an app with your own design: effects and instruments; see [A window of its own](#a-window-of-its-own)):

<!-- guide:run app -->
```sh
npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 new effect-as my-plugin --app
cd my-plugin
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0
npm install
npm run build:ui
npx est validate
npx est test
```

Use a name of your own for `my-plugin` (it becomes the plugin's id, `org.example.my-plugin`, and name; `--id` and `--name` choose them). Then, every time you change something:

1. Change the source (`assembly/index.ts`) and, when the parameters or the identity change, `est.json` and `test/golden.json`.
2. `npx est validate`. It builds, packs `dist/<id>-<version>.est` and runs every check Cyber runs when a plugin is added. **Read `dist/validation.json`**: `ok` is `true` when nothing failed; each entry of `checks` has a `rule` (an id such as `EST-C013`), a `status` (`pass`, `fail`, `warn`), a `message`, a `fix` and often `where`. Fix the first failure, then run it again.
3. When `"ok": true`: `npx est test` renders the golden test in `test/` and runs the conformance run. After changing the sound on purpose, `npx est test --update` takes the new render as the reference.
4. Hear it (below), then tell the person what you built.

`est new` ends by printing a next step with a bare `est` (`est doctor`, `est validate`): run those as `npx est …` inside the folder once the kit is installed there, never as a bare `est` or `npx est` anywhere else.

**What a pass does not prove yet.** @cyber-est/cli 0.1.0's `est validate` does not run `EST-B017`, `EST-M023`, `EST-C024`, `EST-C025`, `EST-C026`, `EST-C027`, `EST-C028`, `EST-C029`, `EST-C030`, `EST-C031`, `EST-C032`, `EST-C033`, `EST-C034`, `EST-C035`, `EST-C036`, `EST-C037`, `EST-C038`, `EST-C039`, `EST-C040`, `EST-U006` (Cyber's later behaviour checks; they never refuse a plugin at Add). Follow their rules in [Every validator rule](#every-validator-rule) anyway, above all the tail (`EST-C028`) and tiny numbers (`EST-C027`).

The plugin to add to Cyber is `dist/<id>-<version>.est`. Raise `version` in `est.json` for every build you hand anyone.

### Inside the folder

`est new` also writes `AGENTS.md` (this plugin's files and rules), `est-validator-rules.json` (every rule with its fix), `est-manifest-1.schema.json`, `est-ui.d.ts` (the window library's types) and the ABI files, and copies the kit's library into `est/` (AssemblyScript) or `est/src/` (Rust): read it for anything this guide does not list; do not edit it.

### More about the loop

Also: `npx est doctor` (what is wrong with this folder or machine, and the fix), `npx est pack` (build and pack only), `npx est profile --json` (which function costs most).

Rule ids are stable; the prefix says where to look: `EST-M` the manifest, `EST-B` the bundle, `EST-W` the WebAssembly module, `EST-C` conformance and behaviour, `EST-U` the window, `EST-P` speed (a warning). `est-validator-rules.json` lists every rule: `id`, `title`, `explain`, `fix`, `severity`.

### Hear it

- With a screen: `npx est dev` opens a page that plays the plugin (add `--port 0 --files-port 0` if a port is taken).
- Without a screen: `npx est dev --json --seconds 5` plays it headless and prints one JSON line an event (it needs Playwright's Chromium; `npx est doctor` says how to get it). Without that browser, **still check**: `test/golden.f32`, written by `npx est test`, is the plugin's real output (every left frame, then every right frame, little-endian float32). Read it and check the level and the shape: silent? clipping? does a knob change it? Tell the person what you checked, and that nobody has listened yet.

## Choosing a template

`npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 new <template> <folder>`. Every template is a working plugin; change it rather than starting empty.

| Template | Kind | Language | What it starts as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cpp-clap` | effect | C++ | A smoothed gain written as a CLAP plugin in C++: the starting point for porting a C++ plugin to EST. |
| `effect-as` | effect | AssemblyScript | A smoothed gain into a resonant filter: the starting point for an EST effect in AssemblyScript. |
| `effect-rust` | effect | Rust | A smoothed gain into a resonant filter: the starting point for an EST effect in Rust. |
| `instrument-as` | instrument | AssemblyScript | Four voices of a saw through a resonant low-pass and an ADSR: the starting point for an EST instrument in AssemblyScript. |
| `instrument-rust` | instrument | Rust | Four voices of a saw through a resonant low-pass and an ADSR: the starting point for an EST instrument in Rust. |
| `midi-effect-as` | effect | AssemblyScript | An arpeggiator synced to the tempo and a chord memory: the starting point for an EST note effect in AssemblyScript. |
| `midi-effect-rust` | effect | Rust | An arpeggiator synced to the tempo and a chord memory: the starting point for an EST note effect in Rust. |
| `sampler-as` | instrument | AssemblyScript | Samples mapped to keys and velocity layers, one-shot or looped, with an ADSR: the starting point for an EST sampler in AssemblyScript. |
| `sampler-rust` | instrument | Rust | Samples mapped to keys and velocity layers, one-shot or looped, with an ADSR: the starting point for an EST sampler in Rust. |
| `visualiser-as` | effect | AssemblyScript | Audio through, and a page that draws the level after it: the starting point for an EST plugin with a visual UI in AssemblyScript. |
| `visualiser-rust` | effect | Rust | Audio through, and a page that draws the level after it: the starting point for an EST plugin with a visual UI in Rust. |

The cookbook's recipes are small finished plugins to start from the same way (`npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 new <recipe> <folder>`):

| Recipe | Kind | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `auto-wah` | effect | An auto-wah: an envelope follower on the input sweeps a resonant band-pass filter up from Base by up to Range octaves. |
| `bitcrusher` | effect | A bitcrusher: the signal quantised to fewer bits and held for several samples, mixed with the dry signal. |
| `chorus` | effect | A stereo chorus: a modulated delay per channel, the two LFOs a quarter-turn apart, mixed with the dry signal. |
| `compressor` | effect | A peak compressor with threshold, ratio, attack, release and make-up gain, its channels linked. |
| `drum-synth` | instrument | A drum synth: a kick (a falling sine), a snare (a tone and noise) and a hat (high-passed noise), on the General MIDI keys. |
| `ring-mod` | effect | A ring modulator: the input multiplied by a sine carrier, mixed with the dry signal. |
| `schroeder-reverb` | effect | A Schroeder reverb: four damped feedback combs in parallel, then two all-passes, per channel, the right a little longer for width. |
| `step-sequencer` | effect | A step sequencer: eight steps of notes from a root key, at a rate synced to the tempo, free or with the transport; notes played in pass through. |
| `wavetable` | instrument | A wavetable synth: four single-cycle waves (sine, triangle, saw, square) morphed by Position, six voices with an envelope. |
| `widener` | effect | A stereo widener: the signal as mid and side, the side scaled by Width (0 % mono, 100 % unchanged, 200 % twice as wide). |

Choose **effect-as** or **instrument-as** unless the person asks for something the others are: a note effect (an arpeggiator) is `midi-effect-as`, a sampler `sampler-as`, a plugin whose point is its picture `visualiser-as`. Pick Rust or C++ only when the person already writes it.

## The commands of @cyber-est/cli 0.1.0

Outside a plugin folder write `npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 <command>`; inside one where the kit is installed, `npx est <command>`. `npx est help <command>` prints a command's options.

| Command | What it does | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| `compare` | Render the same input through two bundles (or a bundle and a desktop WAV) and report how they differ | `est compare <a> <b> [--input <kind\|file.wav>] [--events <json>] [--events-a <json>] [--events-b <json>] [--seconds <n>] [--sample-rate <hz>] [--tolerance <dB>] [--threshold <dB>] [--report <file.html>] [--write-input <file.wav>] [--write-a <file.wav>] [--write-b <file.wav>] [--no-build] [--json]` |
| `dev` | Play a plugin in the dev host while you build it (http://localhost:4430; --json headless) | `est dev [dir \| file.est] [--port 4430] [--files-port 4431] [--no-watch] [--open]`<br>`est dev [dir \| file.est] --json [--seconds N] [--play 60,64,67]`<br>`est dev <folder with ui/> --ui-preview params.json` |
| `doctor` | Check Node, the meter, rustup with wasm32-unknown-unknown, cargo, asc and clang for wasm32; print the command for anything missing | `est doctor [--json]` |
| `inspect` | Show a .est bundle's manifest, files and module (imports, exports, memory, metering) | `est inspect <file.est> [--json] [--no-meter]` |
| `new` | Make a plugin folder from a template (effect, instrument, sampler, midi-effect, visualiser: -rust or -as, cpp-clap) or a cookbook recipe | `est new <template> <dir> [--id <reverse-dns id>] [--name <name>] [--ui \| --app]` |
| `pack` | Build a plugin folder and pack it to dist/<id>-<version>.est | `est pack [dir] [--no-build] [--json]` |
| `profile` | Show where a block's fuel goes, function by function (the functions by fuel, share and calls) | `est profile [dir\|bundle] [--debug] [--seconds <n>] [--notes] [--golden] [--top <n>] [--no-build] [--json]` |
| `test` | Run the plugin's golden render (test/golden.json) and the conformance run | `est test [dir] [--update] [--no-build] [--seconds <n>]` |
| `validate` | Validate a plugin folder (built and packed first) or a .est; writes validation.json | `est validate [dir \| file.est] [--json] [--no-build] [--seconds <n>] [--verbose]` |

The kit's publishing commands are left out on purpose: this guide makes a plugin for the person's own account.

## The manifest, est.json

`est new` writes it; you change the identity, the description and the parameters. `est pack` fills `module`, `ui.sha256` and `assets`. Every field (generated from the schema the validator checks):

| Field | Type | Required | Limits | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `est` | `1` | yes |  | The manifest schema version: 1. |
| `id` | string | yes |  | The plugin's id, a reverse-DNS name (`com.example.my-verb`), the same as its CLAP descriptor's. Never changed: projects name the plugin by it. (EST-M002) |
| `version` | string | yes |  | A semantic version. (EST-M003) |
| `name` | string | yes | ≤ 60 characters | The plugin's name as Cyber shows it. (EST-M004) |
| `vendor` | string | yes | ≤ 60 characters | Who makes it. (EST-M004) |
| `description` | string |  | ≤ 400 characters | One or two plain sentences. (EST-M004) |
| `url` | string |  |  | The plugin's web page, https only. (EST-M004) |
| `contact` | object |  |  | Optional, recommended (1.918): the maker's contact, where feature requests for the plugin are emailed when it has no developer account in Cyber (the first email only asks the address to confirm; every email can stop them). Never shown to anyone. Informational in EST 1.0 and 1.1 alike. (EST-M023) |
| `contact.email` | string |  | ≤ 254 characters | The address, such as you@example.com. |
| `license` | string | yes | ≤ 64 characters | An SPDX licence id or name (`MIT`). (EST-M004) |
| `kind` | `"effect"` or `"instrument"` | yes |  | An effect (audio in, audio out) or an instrument (notes in, audio out). (EST-M005) |
| `features` | array of string | yes | ≥ 1 items, ≤ 32 items | CLAP feature names, the kind's first: `audio-effect` or `instrument`. (EST-M006) |
| `abi` | object | yes |  | (EST-M007) |
| `abi.est` | `"1.0"` or `"1.1"` | yes |  | The EST ABI edition: `1.0`, or (since Cyber 1.327) `1.1` for the fields EST 1.1 adds (a sidechain, up to 8 channels, `modulatable`, `ui.audio`, a preset's `image` and `author`). A newer edition is refused (EST-M019); a 1.1 field in a 1.0 manifest is refused (EST-M020). |
| `abi.clap` | string | yes | ≤ 16 characters | The CLAP version (`1.2`). |
| `module` | object | yes |  | The WebAssembly module. (EST-M008) |
| `module.path` | string | yes | ≤ 255 characters | The module's path in the bundle (`module.wasm`). |
| `module.sha256` | string | yes |  | Filled by `est pack`. |
| `module.bytes` | integer | yes | ≥ 8, ≤ 67108864 | Filled by `est pack`. |
| `ui` | null or object |  |  | A custom UI page, or null (or absent) for the generated UI. (EST-M009) |
| `ui.path` | string | yes | ≤ 255 characters |  |
| `ui.sha256` | string | yes |  | Filled by `est pack`. |
| `ui.size` | object | yes |  |  |
| `ui.resizable` |  |  |  | Read but unused in EST 1.0 (frame protocol 1 has no resize message): the host draws the frame at `size`, never scaled. |
| `ui.audio` | boolean |  | default `false` | EST 1.1 (frame protocol v3): the page may ask for an analysis of the plugin's output (`est.audio()`: magnitudes and RMS at most 30 times a second, never samples). (EST-M020) |
| `assets` | array of object |  |  | Every other file in the bundle, hashed. Written by `est pack`. (EST-M010) |
| `assets[].path` | string | yes | ≤ 255 characters |  |
| `assets[].sha256` | string | yes |  |  |
| `audio` | object | yes |  | One main audio port each way at most; EST 1.1: an effect's inputs may add a sidechain after it. (EST-M011, EST-M021) |
| `audio.inputs` | array of object | yes | ≤ 2 items |  |
| `audio.outputs` | array of object | yes | ≤ 2 items |  |
| `audio.sampleRates` |  |  |  | Informational in EST 1.0: the host does not read it. The templates write "any": a plugin runs at the audio context's rate (44.1 or 48 kHz, whatever the device runs at) and must take whatever `activate` gives it. |
| `notes` | object |  |  | Note ports: 0 or 1 each way; an instrument has a note input. (A value that is not an object is read as none.) (EST-M012) |
| `notes.inputs` | integer |  | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |  |
| `notes.outputs` | integer |  | ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |  |
| `limits` | object |  |  | The most the plugin may use; the host holds it to them. (A value that is not an object is read as the defaults.) (EST-M013) |
| `limits.maxLatencyFrames` | integer |  | ≥ 0, ≤ 192000, default `0` |  |
| `limits.memoryPagesMax` | integer |  | ≥ 1, ≤ 2048, default `256` | 64 KiB pages; the module's declared maximum must be within it. |
| `limits.tailSeconds` | integer |  | ≥ 0, ≤ 60, default `0` |  |
| `permissions` | array of values |  | ≤ 0 items | EST 1.0 grants none: empty. (EST-M014) |
| `parameters` | array of object |  | ≤ 512 items | A mirror of the module's parameters: the same ids. (EST-M015) |
| `parameters[].id` | integer | yes | ≥ 0, ≤ 4294967295 |  |
| `parameters[].name` | string | yes | ≤ 255 characters |  |
| `parameters[].unit` | string |  | ≤ 16 characters |  |
| `parameters[].scale` | `"linear"` or `"log"` |  | default `"linear"` | How knobs, sliders and automation move over the parameter's range: "log" geometrically (a lane's midpoint is the geometric middle; the range the module reports must stay above 0, EST-C021). Since EST 1.286. |
| `parameters[].modulatable` | boolean |  | default `false` | EST 1.1: Cyber's clip envelopes may send this parameter `CLAP_EVENT_PARAM_MOD`; the DSP flags it `CLAP_PARAM_IS_MODULATABLE` (EST-C022). (EST-M020) |
| `stateVersion` | integer |  | ≥ 1, ≤ 1000000, default `1` | The version of the state the plugin saves. (EST-M016) |
| `presets` | null or string |  |  | The bundle's preset index (`presets/index.json`), or null. (EST-M017) |
| `compat` | object |  |  | Informational in EST 1.0: Cyber's reader ignores it. The host versions the bundle is built for (the specification draft's plan: a bundle outside the range installs with a warning and runs). |
| `compat.host` |  |  |  | A semver range of EST host versions; the templates write ">=1.0.0 <2". |
| `migrate` | array of object |  | ≤ 32 items | Since Cyber 1.337: what this version does with the settings a project saved with an earlier version. On Use installed version, Cyber applies the first entry whose `from` takes the version moved from and says what it kept, moved and dropped; without one, settings cross by id as before. A manifest with `migrate` lists its `parameters`. (EST-M022) |
| `migrate[].from` | string | yes | ≤ 100 characters | The versions this entry applies to: comparators separated by spaces, all of which must hold (`>=1.0.0 <1.2.0`), a single version (that one only), or `*` (every version). Versions compare as semver (a pre-release before its release). |
| `migrate[].params` | object |  |  | Old CLAP id (a decimal string) to new id (a renamed or split parameter: the value moves) or `null` (dropped on purpose). Every new id must be one `parameters` lists; an old id named by neither this map nor `parameters` is dropped with a note. |
| `migrate[].state` | `"keep"` or `"drop"` |  | default `"keep"` | Whether the saved state (the CLAP state stream) crosses: `keep` (the plugin reads its earlier versions' state, CLAP's rule) or `drop` (the new version starts from its defaults on purpose, with the mapped values on top). |

An effect's `"notes"` is `{ "inputs": 0, "outputs": 0 }` (a note effect: `"outputs": 1`); an instrument's `{ "inputs": 1, "outputs": 0 }` and its `"audio"` has no inputs. Keep `"parameters"` exactly what the code declares: the same ids, names and ranges (`EST-C008`).

## Writing it in AssemblyScript

### How it is written (AssemblyScript)

- **The export block** at the top of `assembly/index.ts` and the `abort` function at the bottom stay as they are. `describe()` is the identity and the state magic; its first feature (`"audio-effect"` or `"instrument"`) decides the kind.
- **Parameters** are declared once, in `parameters()`, and listed in `est.json`. Values are plain units (dB, Hz, ms), never 0 to 1.
- `paramChanged(id, value)` gets each new value at its own sample. Every default arrives there first, before `activate`, so `activate` sets each block's sample rate and then resets it, as the template does.
- *Effects:* `render(io, from, to)` writes frames `from` to `to`: `io.input(c, n)` in, `io.output(c, n, v)` out.
- *Effects:* `tail()` is how many frames still sound after the input stops; 0 unless something rings.
- *Instruments:* **Notes arrive at their sample**: `noteOn(io, note)`, `noteOff`, `choke`. `Voices<T>` keeps the books: `start(io, note)` gives a free voice or steals the oldest; in `render`, call `end(i, io, n)` the moment a voice falls silent.
- *Instruments:* `render(io, from, to)` **adds** the voices into frames `from` to `to` with `io.add(c, n, v)`: the outputs start each block at zero.
- *Instruments:* `tail()` is the longest a released note sounds (an `Envelope`'s `tailFrames()`), and `limits.tailSeconds` in `est.json` must cover it.
- `saveState(w)` and `loadState(r, version)` add your own bytes after the parameters, which are saved for you.

### The rules

- **Allocate nothing while playing**: not in `render`, `process`, the parameter hook or a note handler.
  - `new`, array literals, strings and closures only in field initialisers, the constructor or `activate`. No top-level code but constants (it would become a start function, which traps: `EST-W`).
- **Be deterministic, import nothing**: the same input and events give the same output, bit for bit. No clock, no file, no host function. For noise, step your own seed, a 32-bit xorshift (`x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >> 17; x ^= x << 5`), set from a constant in `reset`.
- **Size every buffer and time from the sample rate `activate` gives.** The validator runs at 48 kHz; Cyber runs at the device's rate.
- **The ids agree**: the descriptor's id is `est.json`'s `id` (`EST-C001`); the kind and ports match (`EST-C003`, `EST-C004`); each parameter has one numeric id in the code, in `est.json`'s `parameters`, in `test/golden.json`'s events and in the window (`EST-C008`), and it never changes.
- **The state magic** (four characters, where the plugin is described) never changes once anyone has a version.
- **Stay in range**: no output above +18 dBFS, no NaN, memory within `limits.memoryPagesMax` (64 KiB pages).
- **Flush tiny numbers** (`EST-C027`): set a state that feeds itself (a feedback path, a filter's memory, an envelope falling to 0) to 0 once it is below `1e-20`. Flush your own states; the published kit's `Filter` does not flush its own state, and 0.1.0's `est validate` does not run this check.
- *Instruments:* **Every note you start ends**: tell the host when a voice stops sounding (`Voices` does, when you call `end`). A choke stops at once. After the tail the output is silent.
- **Every version is new**: bump `version` in `est.json` for each build you hand to anyone.

### The library on one page (AssemblyScript)

Import everything from `"est"`. Numbers are `f64` unless a type is shown. If a function is not listed here, it does not exist: write the few lines yourself.

The library's source is in `est/`: read it for anything more, do not edit it.

- **Base class**: extend `Effect` or `Instrument`. You must write `render(io: Io, from: i32, to: i32): void`. Optional hooks: `activate(sampleRate: f64, maxFrames: u32): bool`, `reset(): void`, `paramChanged(id: u32, value: f64): void`, `tail(): u32` and `latency(): u32` (frames), `event(io: Io, e: Event): void`, `saveState(w: StateWriter): void`, `loadState(r: StateReader, version: u32): bool`.
- **`Io`**: `io.channels: i32`, `io.frames: i32`, `io.input(c: i32, n: i32): f32`, `io.output(c, n, v: f32)`, `io.add(c, n, v: f32)`, `io.param(id: u32): f64`, `io.transport`.
- *Instruments and note effects:* **Note hooks**: `noteOn(io: Io, note: Note): void`, `noteOff` and `choke` (the same arguments). Out: `io.noteEnd(id: i32, port: i16, channel: i16, key: i16, n: i32)`, `io.sendNoteOn(id: i32, channel: i16, key: i16, velocity: f64, n: i32)`, `io.sendNoteOff` (the same arguments).
- *Instruments and note effects:* **`Note`** fields: `time: i32` (its frame in the block), `noteId: i32` (-1: none), `port: i16`, `channel: i16`, `key: i16`, `velocity: f64` (0 to 1). There is no `id` field. Cast before maths: `keyToHz(<f64>note.key)`.
- **`Transport`** fields: `tempo: f64`, `playing: bool`, `beat: f64`, `barStart: f64`, `num: u16`, `den: u16`.
- **`Event`** fields: `kind` (`EventKind.Param`, `NoteOn`, `NoteOff`, `Choke`, `Transport` …), `time: i32`, `id: u32`, `value: f64`, `note`, `transport`.
- **`Param`**: `new Param(id: u32, "Name")`, then `.range(min, max)`, `.default(v)`, `.unit("dB")`, `.decimals(n)`, `.hertz()`, `.log()`, `.labels(["A", "B"])` (a switch: values 0, 1 …), `.module("Group")`, `.bypass()`, `.hidden()`, `.readOnly()`.
- **`Descriptor`**: `new Descriptor(id, name, vendor, version, description, features: string[], stateMagic, stateVersion: u32)`; `.noteEffect()` for notes out.
- **Maths**: `dbToGain(db)`, `gainToDb(gain)`, `keyToHz(key)`, `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `exp(x)`, `ln(x)`, `exp2(x)`, `log2(x)`, `floor(x)`, `round(x)`, `sinTurns(t)` and `cosTurns(t)` (`t` in turns: 1 is a whole cycle), `tanHalfTurns(t)`, `onePole(seconds, sampleRate)` (a smoothing coefficient). The language's own `Math.sqrt`, `Math.abs`, `Math.sin`, `Math.tanh`, `Math.pow` and `Math.exp` also work; never `Math.random`.
- **`Smoother`**: `new Smoother(seconds)`; `setSampleRate(sr)`, `setTime(seconds)`, `setTarget(v)`, `jump(v)`, `reset()` (jump to the target), `next(): f64` once a sample, `settled(): bool`.
- **`Filter`** (state-variable, one per channel): `setSampleRate(sr)`, `setMode(FilterMode.Low)` (or `Band`, `High`, `Notch`; `filterModeFromIndex(v)`), `setCutoff(hz)`, `setResonance(r)` (0 to 1), `setSmoothing(seconds)`, `reset()`, `process(x: f64): f64`.
- **`Biquad`**: `set(BiquadKind.Peak, freq, q, gainDb, sampleRate)` (or `LowShelf`, `HighShelf`, `LowPass`, `HighPass`), `reset()`, `process(x: f64): f64`.
- **`DelayLine`** (`f64` in and out): `allocate(maxFrames: i32): bool` in `activate`, `clear()`; each sample, `read(delayFrames: f64): f64` **before** `write(x: f64)`. The shortest delay is 1 frame; a fraction is interpolated.
- **`Oscillator`**: `setSampleRate(sr)`, `setFrequency(hz)`, `setWave(Wave.Sine)` (or `Saw`, `Square`, `Triangle`; `waveFromIndex(v)`), `reset(phase)`, `next(): f64` (-1 to 1).
- **`Lfo`**: `setSampleRate(sr)`, `setRate(hz)`, `setSync(beats)` (0: free), `setTempo(bpm)`, `setWave(Wave.Sine)`, `reset(phase)`, `next(): f64` (-1 to 1).
- **`Envelope`** (ADSR): `setSampleRate(sr)`, `setAdsr(attack, decay, sustain, release)` (seconds; sustain 0 to 1) or `setAttack`, `setDecay`, `setSustain`, `setRelease`; `start()`, `release()`, `reset()`, `next(): f64`, `isActive(): bool`, `tailFrames(): u32`.
- *Instruments and note effects:* **`Voices<T>`**: `new Voices<MyVoice>(n)` in a field initialiser; `start(io, note): i32` (the voice's index), `release(note)`, `choke(io, note)`, `voice(i): T`, `note(i): Note`, `isOn(i): bool`, `end(i, io, n)`, `reset()`. A voice class extends `Voice`, has a constructor with no arguments, and overrides `release(): void` and `stop(): void`.
- **State**: `w.u32(v)`, `w.f32(v)`, `w.f64(v)`; `r.u32()`, `r.f32()`, `r.f64()`.

### What costs time

`npx est validate` reports a block's mean cost and warns past 100 µs (`EST-P001`, a warning only). The warning is the best of three runs, so the cost is real (`npx est profile --json` names the function). The usual causes:

- **A sine a sample.** `sinTurns`, `cosTurns`, a sine `Oscillator` and a sine `Lfo` each sum a series with a division per term. One LFO is fine; one per voice adds up. Cheaper: a triangle or saw `Lfo`, your own phase with a parabola, or one value every 16 frames, smoothed.
- **A gliding `Filter`** works out its coefficients again every sample while its cutoff or resonance moves. If you move the cutoff all the time (an envelope, an LFO), call `setSmoothing(0)` once and `setCutoff` every 16 frames.
- **`DelayLine`'s `read` with a fraction** interpolates: a chorus needs it, a plain echo can round its delay to whole frames.
- **`exp`, `ln`, `dbToGain`, `keyToHz` a sample.** Work them out in `paramChanged` or at the note's start, and smooth the result.

### Following the song

The transport (tempo, beat, playing) is **as of the block's first sample**, or of a transport event inside the block. It does not move while you render: keep your own beat and add `tempo / 60 / sampleRate` each sample while it plays. With no transport event `playing` is false, and `npx est validate` and the default golden render run that way.

To prove a plugin that follows the tempo, put a transport event in `test/golden.json`'s `events` (every field is needed; `time` in seconds):

```json
{ "type": "transport", "time": 0, "tempo": 120, "beat": 0, "seconds": 0, "num": 4, "den": 4, "barStart": 0, "barNumber": 0, "playing": true }
```

Count bars from `barStart`, never from beat 0.

### A delay or a reverb

- **Memory.** A `DelayLine` holds 4 bytes a frame: a second of stereo at 96 kHz is about 12 pages of 64 KiB. Raise `maximumMemory` in `asconfig.json` and `limits.memoryPagesMax` in `est.json` **together** (both in pages; 64 covers a few seconds).
- **The tail.** Report how long it rings, in frames, from `tail()`, and keep `limits.tailSeconds` in `est.json` at least that long. It may be 60 at most: cap the feedback (or the time) so it dies inside that. `EST-C028` fails a plugin that still sounds after the tail it reports; it tests with the song stopped at 60 BPM, where a tempo-synced echo is longest.
- *Effects:* **Noise of its own.** An effect that sounds with silence in (hiss, crackle) trips `EST-C028` too: fade it out when the input stops.

### Easy to get wrong

- **A frequency or time knob** wants a log scale: `.log()` on the parameter and `"scale": "log"` on its row in `est.json`'s `parameters`.
- **A switch or chooser** (`.labels`) shows its labels on Cyber's knobs: at most 64 steps, 32 characters a label.
- **Smooth every level and cutoff change** (`Smoother`), or a moving knob clicks.
- **`test/golden.json`'s events name parameters by id** (`{ "type": "param", "time": 0.1, "id": 1, "value": 800 }`: plain units, seconds). Change them when a parameter changes, then `npx est test --update`.
- *Instruments and note effects:* **A note in `test/golden.json`**: `{ "type": "noteOn", "time": 0.1, "key": 60, "channel": 0, "port": 0, "noteId": 1, "velocity": 0.8 }`, then a `noteOff` with the same `noteId`.
- **`test/golden.f32`** is every left frame, then every right frame (little-endian float32), not interleaved.
- **validate's `peak`** is the stress run's worst case, not the level at the defaults.

### The golden test

`test/golden.json` says what `est test` renders and compares with `test/golden.f32`:

- `"input"`: an effect's input signal. The kinds that make sound in 0.1.0: `{ "kind": "noise", "seed": 1, "level": 0.5 }`. **Any other kind renders silence without a word** (an `"impulse"` or `"sine"` there stores a silent reference that then always passes), so keep one of these. An instrument's input is silence; its sound comes from note events.
- `"frames"`: the length, **a multiple of 128** (`12288` is 0.256 s at 48 kHz).
- `"events"`: parameter changes and notes, `time` in seconds, values in plain units.
- Changing `frames`, the events, the input or the sound makes the next `npx est test` fail (a different length, or samples that differ): check the change is what you meant, then `npx est test --update`.

**To see what an effect does to a single hit** (an echo's repeats, a reverb's decay), which the golden noise hides: `npx est compare dist/<id>-<version>.est dist/<id>-<version>.est --input impulse --write-a impulse.wav` writes the impulse response as a WAV. Read it: the repeats' spacing, level and brightness.

### Values and units

- A parameter's value is in the unit it shows: dB, Hz, ms, and a percentage as 0 to 100 (`45` is 45 %), never 0 to 1 unless the unit is a plain factor.
- **An echo's tail**: with delay time *T* seconds and feedback gain *g* (0 to 1), the repeats fall below −60 dB after about *T* × 3 / log10(1/*g*) seconds (*g* 0.9 at 1.5 s: about 98 s, too long). Report it from `tail()` in frames, keep it at most 60 s (`limits.tailSeconds`), and lower the most feedback at long times so it fits.

### The budget

Each audio block runs on fuel: the meter charges by work, and a block that runs out of fuel is stopped. Cyber also bypasses a plugin whose blocks stay over budget. `npx est validate` reports a block's cost (`EST-P001` warns past the budget); `npx est profile --json` names the function that costs most. Work out anything expensive when a parameter changes or a note starts, never per sample.

## Rust and C or C++

Use these only when the person already writes the language. Run `npx est doctor` first: it names the toolchain to install (Rust: `rustup` with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target; C and C++: clang 16 or newer with the WebAssembly target). The loop, the manifest, the rules and the window are the same.

#### How it is written (Rust)

- **The plugin** is one `impl Effect` or `impl Instrument` in `src/lib.rs` and one `est::export_effect!`, `est::export_instrument!` or `est::export_note_effect!` at the bottom: the macro's `id` is the identity, and the macro decides the kind. `use est::prelude::*;` brings the library.
- **Parameters** are declared once, in `PARAMS`, and listed in `est.json`. Values are plain units (dB, Hz, ms), never 0 to 1.
- `param_changed(id, value)` gets each new value at its own sample. Every default arrives there first, before `activate`, so `activate` sets each block's sample rate and then resets it, as the template does.
- `new()` builds the plugin by value and allocates nothing; `activate(sample_rate, max_frames)` is the only place to allocate.
- *Effects:* `render(io, from, to)` writes frames `from..to`: `io.input(c, n)` in, `io.output(c, n, v)` out.
- *Effects:* `tail()` is how many frames still sound after the input stops; 0 unless something rings.
- *Instruments:* **Notes arrive at their sample**: `note_on(io, note)`, `note_off`, `choke`. `Voices<T, N>` keeps the books: `start(io, note)` gives a free voice or steals the oldest; in `render`, call `end(i, io, n)` the moment a voice falls silent.
- *Instruments:* `render(io, from, to)` **adds** the voices into frames `from..to` with `io.add(c, n, v)`: the outputs start each block at zero.
- *Instruments:* `tail()` is the longest a released note sounds (an `Envelope`'s `tail_frames()`), and `limits.tailSeconds` in `est.json` must cover it.
- `STATE_MAGIC` is four bytes (`u32::from_le_bytes(*b"ABCD")`); `save_state` and `load_state` add your own bytes after the parameters, which are saved for you.

The Rust library is in the folder's `est/src/` (`use est::prelude::*;`): the same blocks as AssemblyScript's under snake_case names (`db_to_gain`, `key_to_hz`, `Smoother`, `Filter`, `DelayLine`, `Envelope`, `Voices`). Read it there.

#### How it is written (C and C++)

- **`est.json` is the only file that names the plugin**: the build writes `build/est_plugin.h` from it, and the descriptor reads `EST_PLUGIN_ID`. Never write the id in the source.
- **The DSP** is plain C++ in `src/gain.hpp`: no CLAP, no allocation. Replace it with yours; it may be the same file a desktop build compiles.
- **The CLAP side** is `src/plugin.cpp`: the entry, the factory, the descriptor, `kParams`, `process`, `clap.params`, `clap.state`, `clap.audio-ports`, `clap.latency`.
- **Parameters** are declared once, in `kParams` (id, name, module, min, max, default, flags, unit), and listed in `est.json`. Values are plain units (dB, Hz), never 0 to 1.
- **Events are sample accurate**: `Plugin::process` runs the DSP between two events and applies each at its frame. Add your event types in `handleEvent` (for an instrument: `CLAP_EVENT_NOTE_ON` and the rest, and set `kind` and `notes.inputs` in `est.json`).
- **`activate`** is the only place to allocate: delay lines, tables.
- **The state** is `kStateMagic`, `kStateVersion`, then every parameter.
- **The toolchain**: any clang 16 or newer with the WebAssembly target and `wasm-ld` (`npx est doctor` says what is missing). `est` calls clang directly, never the `emcc` driver, which adds imports EST refuses. `EST_CLANG=/path/to/clang++` picks one.
- **Check a port against the original**: `npx est compare dist/<id>-<version>.est reference.wav --input input.wav`, with a render from the desktop build.
- **What does not come across**: a native window toolkit (the window is a web page), threads, files, the network.

## A window of its own

Cyber draws knobs from the parameters, and that is enough to start. A window of your own is a web page in the bundle (`ui/index.html`, named by `"ui"` in `est.json`), never a native one: scripts as files, nothing from another host, no `fetch`. The `EST-U` rules in `est-validator-rules.json` say what a page may hold, and `est-ui.d.ts` has the page library's types.

Two ways to make one, each from `npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 new`:

### `--ui`: a page with knobs

In a folder made with `new <template> <folder> --ui`:

This folder has a window in `ui/` (`ui/index.html`, `ui/ui.js`, `ui/style.css`): an `<est-knob>` for each parameter, and `est.json`'s `"ui"` entry. Change the page to match your parameters.

- `ui/index.html` loads `<script src="est-ui.js"></script>` and then your script, both as files. `npx est pack` copies `est-ui.js` into the bundle: do not add it yourself. It gives `EstUI.connect()`, `EstUI.bind(el, id)` and the `<est-knob param="ID">` and `<est-slider>` elements; `est-ui.d.ts` has its types.
- `est.json`: `"ui": { "path": "ui/index.html", "size": { "w": 440, "h": 180 } }`. Cyber draws the frame at exactly that size (CSS pixels) and never scales it.
- What loads: scripts, CSS, `.png`, `.webp` and `.svg` images and `.woff2` fonts that are files of the bundle (inline `<style>` too). No inline script, no `.jpg` or `.gif`, nothing from another host, no `fetch`. The `EST-U` rules check it.
- `npx est dev` shows the page beside the generated knobs. `npx est dev --json` reports it as `ui` lines: its load, `est:ready`, each message the host refused and why, console errors and files that did not load.
- A plugin other people add shows its own window only once Cyber has reviewed it; until then they see the generated knobs, so keep every control a parameter.

### `--app`: a small web app (effects and instruments)

In a folder made with `new <template> <folder> --app` (the third block of [The loop](#the-loop)):

This folder's window is an app: `ui-app/` is its source, and `npm run build:ui` builds it into `ui/`, the page `est.json`'s `"ui"` names. Change the app in `ui-app/`, never in `ui/`: the build empties `ui/` each time. Then `npx est validate` and `npx est dev` as usual.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | `npm run build:ui`, and `npm run dev:ui` (the app in a plain browser with a stand-in engine) |
| `ui-app/vite.config.ts` | The build: one classic script, relative URLs, fonts from the script, other hosts cut out |
| `ui-app/index.html` | The page; its `est-ui-size` meta gave `est.json`'s `ui.size` |
| `ui-app/main.ts` | The example app, no framework: a slider per parameter. Replace it with yours |
| `ui-app/store.ts` | The app's state: the app reads and writes only this |
| `ui-app/bridge.ts` | The link to the host: `applyHost`, `pushStore` (a drag is one gesture), `decodeReadout` |
| `ui-app/engine.ts` | The stand-in for `npm run dev:ui`; the build swaps it for `bridge.ts` |
| `ui-app/bits.ts` | `packFields` and `unpackFields`: the app's own data in hidden parameters |
| `ui-app/fonts.ts` | `registerFonts`: a font imported as `?base64` and registered from its bytes |

What the frame needs (the build does it, and `npx est validate` checks it):

- **One classic script**: no `<script type="module">`, no `crossorigin`, no `modulepreload` (`EST-U005`), or the frame stays blank.
- **Nothing from another host** (`EST-U002`), and never `fetch`: put the data the app needs in the script.
- **Fonts in the script**: import each as `?base64` and call `registerFonts`.
- **The host plays.** The sound, the transport, the keys and the tempo are Cyber's: no play button or keyboard in the app.
- **Every piece of state is a parameter** (up to 512): knobs are ordinary ones, the app's own data `hidden()` ones packed with `bits.ts`, what the plugin is playing `hidden().readOnly()` ones the DSP sets.
- **The size is fixed**: change the `est-ui-size` meta and `est.json`'s `ui.size` together.

### What every window must do

- **It talks to the plugin only through messages.** `EstUI.connect()` gives the connection: each parameter's value, changes both ways, gestures (press, drag, release as one), meters. The frame never receives audio samples: a meter or spectrum comes from the host's own messages.
- **It fills its frame.** Lay the page out at its `ui.size` (CSS pixels) with no empty band; Cyber may draw it narrower or, popped out, larger: let the controls take the space, never a stretched picture.
- **Fonts come from bytes**: put a font in the bundle as a file and register it with `FontFace` from its bytes (the `--app` template's `registerFonts` does). A `@font-face` with a `url()` cannot load in the sandboxed frame.
- **Readable**: text at a contrast of at least 4.5:1 against what is behind it.
- **Every control has a name** (a label, or `aria-label`) and is reachable by Tab; a knob is a `role="slider"` with its value as text.
- **Reduced motion**: under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing moves but what the sound itself moves.
- **Nothing flashes** more than three times a second.
- **The host owns the keys and the transport**: no play button or on-screen keyboard; take only the keys a control needs.
- **A window is optional and secondary**: a plugin other people add shows its own window only once Cyber has reviewed it (until then, Cyber's generated knobs), so every control must be a parameter.

## Presets and levels

- **A preset is a state**: a file in the bundle's `presets/` folder, listed in `presets/index.json` (`{ "presets": [ { "name", "path", "tags": [], "stateVersion" } ] }`) and named by `est.json`'s `"presets": "presets/index.json"`. Each file is exactly the bytes the plugin's own state save writes. The kit has no command that writes them, so leave `"presets"` out unless you write those bytes yourself; the person saves their own presets in Cyber, in every EST plugin's preset row.
- **Name presets `Category · Name`** (Cyber's preset browser groups by the part before ` · `).
- **Level-match by gain, never by compressing**: give the plugin an output or level parameter and set each preset's level so they sound equally loud; a preset should not be louder just to sound better.
- `EST-C012` (a preset that does not load) and `EST-C019` (a preset that does not save back its own bytes) check them.

## Every validator rule

Generated from the rules Cyber checks. **At add** means Cyber refuses a plugin that fails it when the person adds it; the others are the kit's own checks (a speed warning, the window, determinism, behaviour). Rule ids never change. The folder's `est-validator-rules.json` has each rule's full explanation.

| Rule | Severity | At add | What it means | The fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EST-B001` | error | yes | **Not a canonical EST archive.** A .est bundle is a ZIP archive in one exact shape (spec §2): its entries from byte 0, the central directory and its end record straight after, no archive comment, no ZIP64, one disk. Anything else could hide data a reader would skip, so the host refuses it before reading a file. | Pack the bundle with `est pack` (or @cyber-est/tools' `pack`), never with a general ZIP tool, and do not edit the .est afterwards. |
| `EST-B002` | error | yes | **An entry is not stored plainly.** Every entry is stored uncompressed, unencrypted and without a data descriptor, with its sizes in its own header; a directory entry has no data. This keeps one set of files to one archive and lets the plugin origin serve the files as they are. | Pack with `est pack`, which stores every file plainly. |
| `EST-B003` | error | yes | **Damaged archive records.** A local header disagrees with its central directory record, or a record runs past the archive's data: the bundle is damaged or was altered after packing. | Pack the bundle again with `est pack` and copy the new file whole. |
| `EST-B004` | error | yes | **The bundle is too large.** A bundle is at most 64 MiB and 512 entries, and its est.json at most 256 KiB, so an install cannot exhaust the device. | Remove files the plugin does not need (build output, sources, large samples), or shrink them. |
| `EST-B005` | error | yes | **A path EST does not allow.** Paths inside a bundle are relative, `/`-separated segments of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` in UTF-8: no absolute path, no `..` or `.`, no backslash, at most 255 characters. The host serves the files under the bundle's hash, and a path outside these rules could escape it or mean different files on different systems. | Rename the file (letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` only) and pack again. |
| `EST-B006` | error | yes | **A symbolic link in the bundle.** An entry is marked as a symbolic link. A bundle holds files only: a link could point outside the bundle when it is unpacked. | Replace the link with the file itself (copy it) and pack again. |
| `EST-B007` | error | yes | **A path is in the bundle twice.** Two entries have the same path, or paths that differ only in case (which name one file on Windows and macOS). | Rename one of the files so every path is unique ignoring case. |
| `EST-B008` | error | yes | **est.json is not the first entry.** The manifest is the archive's first entry, so a reader finds it without scanning the bundle. | Pack with `est pack`, which writes est.json first. |
| `EST-B009` | error | yes | **A file does not match its CRC-32.** An entry's data does not match the CRC-32 its header records: the bundle was damaged in transfer or altered after packing. | Copy the bundle again, or pack it again with `est pack`. |
| `EST-B010` | error | yes | **No est.json, or est.json is not JSON.** Every bundle has a manifest, est.json, in UTF-8 JSON. | Add est.json at the plugin's root (start from a template's), check it parses, and pack again. |
| `EST-B011` | error | yes | **A file is in the bundle but not in est.json.** Every file in the bundle is listed and hashed in est.json (the module, the UI page or an asset), so nothing unlisted can ride along. | Pack with `est pack`, which lists and hashes every file; or remove the stray file. |
| `EST-B012` | error | yes | **est.json lists a file the bundle lacks, or lists one twice.** est.json names a file (the module, the UI page, an asset or the preset index) that is not in the archive, or names one path twice. | Check the paths in est.json against the plugin folder, then pack again with `est pack`. |
| `EST-B013` | error | yes | **A file does not match its SHA-256 in est.json.** A file's SHA-256 (or the module's size) differs from what est.json records: est.json was written for other files, or a file changed after packing. | Pack again with `est pack`, which fills every hash from the files as they are. |
| `EST-B014` | error | yes | **The preset index is not valid.** The preset index named by est.json's `presets` (spec §6) is a JSON file of at most 64 KiB, `{ "presets": [{ "name", "path", "tags", "stateVersion" }] }`, at most 128 presets, each a state file in the bundle of 1 byte to the inline state limit, with a state version no newer than the manifest's. | Fix the entry the message names in the preset index (write the presets with the template's preset script), and pack again. |
| `EST-B015` | error | yes | **Not the bundle asked for.** The bundle's content hash (the SHA-256 of the archive) differs from the hash the host asked for: a different build, or an altered copy. | Install the bundle by its published hash, or install the file itself in developer mode. |
| `EST-B016` | error | yes | **A preset's picture or author is not valid.** In EST 1.1 a preset in the index may name an `image`, a WebP file in the bundle of at most 64 KiB and 1024 × 1024 pixels (the Presets tab shows it), and an `author` in plain text (60 characters). A 1.0 bundle's presets have neither. | Save the picture as `.webp` (at most 64 KiB, e.g. 256 × 256), put it in `presets/`, and name it by its path; or remove `image`. |
| `EST-B017` | error | yes | **A plugin's source, not a built bundle.** The file is a plugin's source packed as a .est (a zip with an AssemblyScript source and no WebAssembly module), as a chat assistant writes one. Only Cyber's Add a plugin file builds a source .est; everywhere else a .est must be a built bundle, so a source one is refused and never compiled there. | Add it with Add a plugin file in Cyber, which builds it in your browser; then Save its .est file gives you a built one to share. With the kit, build the folder with `est pack`. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |

EST-C017 checks one held note at install; this checks the loudest case, every reverb and echo included, and at a slow tempo. | Report a tail that covers everything that can still sound: the longest release, the reverb's decay at its current size, and an echo's repeats at the current tempo (repeats × delay until 60 dB down). Ask for the tempo each block when it depends on it. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C029` | warning |  | **A render from a bar differs from playing through it.** A pattern plugin is played from beat 0 and, fresh, from beat 8 (bar 3), with the transport alone. Once what played before beat 8 has rung out (2 s, or its reported tail and 0.5 s, at most 8 s), the two renders must agree within 1 % RMS: a render or an export that starts at a bar must sound as playing through it does. Randomness seeded by a count of notes or hits, or modulation and noise running from activate, make them differ. | Seed every random choice from the song position (the step, the bar, the pad), never from a count of notes or hits or the time since the plugin started, and restart free-running generators from the position when the transport starts. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C030` | warning |  | **A transport jump fires every skipped step.** A pattern plugin plays from beat 0; at beat 4 the transport jumps to beat 36. In the next 100 ms its output must have at most twice the energy of a start at beat 36 plus the ring-out of what played before: a step clock that catches up step by step after a forward jump fires every skipped step at once, a burst of 128 hits in a few milliseconds. | When the position moves forwards by more than a step (or backwards at all), move the next step to the first one at or after the new position without firing the steps in between. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C031` | warning |  | **It makes no sound, or changes nothing.** An instrument is played five notes (keys 36, 48, 60, 72 and 84 at velocity 0.8) and a soft one (key 60 at 0.25), with the transport stopped and, if all were silent, playing; an effect is given the test loop. Reported: every note silent (under -80 dBFS); some keys silent (unless the plugin's features say it is a drum kit or a sampler); the soft note silent where the same note played harder sounds; an effect whose output is silent, or is its input sample for sample at its defaults and with every parameter at either end. | Start a voice and its envelope on every note-on and add every voice to both outputs; work a key's pitch out for every key; write the processed sample (not the input) to an effect's output, and read each parameter where it is used. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C032` | warning |  | **A note never stops, or the sound never dies away.** A three-note chord is held for half a second and released (an effect: a second of the test loop, then nothing), and the output is listened to for 6.5 s. Reported when, in the last second, it is still over -50 dB of its held level and no quieter than nine tenths of the second before (under 1 dB a second: it is not a long release, it is not ending), and the plugin does not sound by itself with nothing played. EST-C024 and EST-C028 look at NOTE_ENDs and the reported tail; this looks at the sound. | Let a released voice's envelope reach 0 and end the voice there (no floor above 0, no oscillator outside a voice); keep every feedback amount below 1 where it is used, not only where it is set. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C033` | warning |  | **Dangerously loud at its defaults.** A four-note chord at full velocity held for a second (an effect: the test loop, which peaks at -6 dBFS), at the default settings: the plugin's own peak before the host's clamp. Over +9.5 dBFS it is dangerous to hear on headphones (the host clamps at +12); over +6 dBFS it is twice full scale and clips whatever comes after it. The install's own limit (EST-C015) is +18 dBFS, where the host must protect the graph; this is where a person's ears are. | Aim a full chord's peak near -6 dBFS: scale the sum of the voices (by a quarter, or by the voice count's square root), lower the default level, and clamp the final sample to -1…1. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C034` | warning |  | **A DC offset in the output.** The mean of each output channel over half a second of the held chord (an effect: the test loop): past 0.05 either way the output sits off centre, which wastes headroom, thumps when the sound starts and stops, and pushes every compressor and limiter after it. | Remove what adds a constant (a unipolar oscillator or LFO mixed into the output, a waveshaper's offset), or pass the output through a DC blocker: y = x - x1 + 0.995 × y1. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C035` | warning |  | **Output that is not a number, or that the host limits.** At the default settings, on the same chord or loop: a sample that is NaN or infinity (the host writes 0 for it, so the sound drops out), or one past the ±4 (+12 dBFS) where the host clamps a plugin's output and its card says "Output limited". The install refuses only what the conformance signal happens to reach; this is the plugin as a person first plays it. | Guard every division and square root, clamp filter cutoffs to 20 Hz…0.45 × the sample rate, keep resonance below self-oscillation and feedback below 1, and scale the output as EST-C033 says. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C036` | warning |  | **A note ends with a click.** One note (key 60, full velocity) is released at two moments, so at two phases of its wave. Reported when, both times, the output steps in one sample by more than a fifth of the note's held level and more than four times its largest step while it was held: the voice was cut at the note-off instead of faded. A wave with steps of its own (a square, a saw, noise) is not judged. | Give every voice a release of at least a few milliseconds and end it when its envelope reaches 0, never at the note-off itself; a choke may be immediate. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C037` | warning |  | **Too heavy to run.** The fuel a 128-frame block spends (the meter's count of work, the same on every machine) with 1, 8 and 16 notes held (an effect: full-scale noise as its input), as a share of the block's budget. The host stops an instance whose blocks each use 90 % of it; every plugin Cyber ships stays under 75 %. Reported from 75 % (it plays, but close to the limit) and as serious from 90 %, or when the host stopped it. With a profiling build (`est profile`'s meter) the functions that spent the most are named. | Do less per sample in the functions named: compute coefficients once a block or on a parameter change, replace per-sample sin, exp and pow with a phase accumulator or a table, cap the voices and the unison, and have no per-sample loop whose length grows with a parameter. `est profile` shows where the fuel goes. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C038` | warning |  | **A control does nothing.** In a plugin of at most twelve parameters (not hidden, read-only or the bypass), each is set to its minimum and its maximum on a 1.2 s phrase (an instrument: four notes, two of them overlapping at different velocities, releases, the transport playing; an effect: the test loop) and the output compared with the defaults'. One that changes nothing is tried again, at each end, three times with every other parameter at seeded random values (a depth at 0 or a mode switched off hides a control that works). Reported, as a note: the parameters that never changed a sample. A larger plugin's controls depend on modes and on time in ways a second cannot show, so there nothing is said; nor for a drum kit or a sampler (each sound has its own key and controls) or an analyser (its controls are its display's). | Store the value in the parameter's setter and read it in render() where it applies; remove a parameter the sound does not use, from the sound code, est.json and the window. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C039` | warning |  | **The controls together break the sound.** On the same phrase: every parameter at its maximum, at its minimum, and two seeded mixes of ends. Reported when the plugin stops (a trap) or its output is not a number there, and not at the defaults; the parameters it takes are found by putting each back to its default in turn. The conformance run moves one parameter at a time, so it never sees what two do together: a division by a count that another control makes 0, an index worked out from two. | Guard what the parameters reach together where the values are used: divisions by a count or a length, indexes and buffer lengths, a filter with cutoff and resonance both at their ends, a feedback that passes 1. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-C040` | warning |  | **Pitch or time follows the sample rate.** The same note (A4), and for an effect a single click, at 48 kHz and at 44.1 kHz. Reported when the note's period, its release (the time to fall 40 dB) or the click's strongest echo is the same count of frames at both rates, so 8.8 % apart in seconds: a pitch or a time sized as a constant of frames. A sound with no clear pitch, a release under 150 ms and an echo under 96 frames are not judged. The parity suite (1.342) proves Cyber's own plugins sample for sample; this is the cheap form for a plugin just added. | Size every time and frequency from the rate activate gives: frames = seconds × sampleRate, a phase step = frequency / sampleRate, a coefficient = exp(-1 / (seconds × sampleRate)). Never a constant 44100 or 48000. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-U001` | error |  | **The UI page is not readable HTML.** The page est.json's `ui.path` names is UTF-8 HTML. | Save the page as UTF-8 with an `<html>` element (start from a template's `ui/index.html`). |
| `EST-U002` | error |  | **The UI reaches an external host.** A plugin UI runs in a sandboxed frame on the plugin origin and may load only files from its own bundle: a URL to another host (`http:`, `https:`, `//host`, `ws:`) in its HTML, scripts or styles would not load, and is refused so a UI cannot phone home. | Copy the file into the bundle (in `ui/`) and refer to it by a relative path; for @cyber-est/ui use the `ui/est-ui.js` that `est pack` copies. |
| `EST-U003` | error |  | **A UI URL outside the bundle.** Every URL in the UI's HTML, scripts and styles is relative and names a file in the bundle: a root-relative (`/x`) or escaping (`../../x`) URL, or one to a missing file, does not resolve inside the bundle's folder on the plugin origin. | Use a relative path to a file inside the bundle (`ui.js`, `img/knob.png`), and check the file is packed. |
| `EST-U004` | warning |  | **The UI is large.** The UI's files total more than 4 MiB; every install downloads and stores them. | Compress images, drop unused fonts and source maps, and minify scripts. |
| `EST-U005` | error |  | **The UI page loads a module script.** A UI page with a `<script type="module">`, a `crossorigin` attribute on any element or a `<link rel="modulepreload">` shows a blank frame: the frame's origin is opaque (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`), so a module script, a module preload and a `crossorigin` load are CORS requests, which the plugin origin does not answer. A bundler's default page (Vite's) has all three. (1.335) | Load a classic script: build the app into one `iife` bundle and load it with `<script defer src="assets/app.js">`, with no `type="module"`, no `crossorigin` and no `modulepreload` (see ui.md, "A whole app as the window"; `est new … --app` scaffolds a Vite build that does this). |
| `EST-U006` | warning |  | **The window names a parameter the plugin lacks.** The window's files are read as text (never run): every `param="<id>"` attribute of its page (the kit's `<est-knob>` and `<est-slider>`) and every literal id given to the script's API (`get`, `set`, `param`, `begin`, `end` on what `EstUI.connect()` returned) must be the id of a parameter the running plugin reports. A window written apart from the sound code often keeps a control for a parameter the sound dropped, or counts from 1: the control moves and nothing happens. An id built at run time is not seen. (1.914) | Use the same ids in the window and the sound code (they start at 0), and remove a control whose parameter is gone. *(Not in the published kit 0.1.0's `est validate` yet; Cyber's later checks use it.)* |
| `EST-P001` | warning |  | **A block costs more than the budget.** The mean cost of one 128-frame block in the conformance run, metered, on the validating machine, against a budget of 100 µs (about 4 % of the block's real time at 48 kHz). A warning only in Phase 4: the budget is recorded, not enforced, and the number depends on the machine. | Profile `process`: avoid per-sample divisions, `pow` and `exp` (smooth instead), and recomputing coefficients that have not changed. |

## Common failures and their fixes

| You see | Why | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `EST-W004`, an import such as `env.seed` or `env.abort` | `Math.random`, `Date`, `console` or a library call made the module import a host function | Remove it. For noise, step your own xorshift seed set in `reset()`; keep the template's `abort` function at the bottom. |
| `EST-W015`, a start function | Code at the top level (an array, a `new`, a call) runs at start | Keep only constants at the top level; build everything in field initialisers, the constructor or `activate`. |
| `EST-C013`, it stopped while processing | A trap: out of fuel, allocating in `render()`, an index out of range | Move every `new`, array and string out of `render`, `paramChanged` and note handlers; check buffer indices; `npx est profile --json` for fuel. |
| `EST-C001`, it does not start | The descriptor's id differs from `est.json`'s `id`, or `activate` returned false | Use one id in both; size buffers from `activate`'s sample rate. |
| `EST-C008`, the parameters differ | The code and `est.json`'s `parameters` disagree | Same ids, names, ranges and defaults in both, and in `test/golden.json`'s events. |
| `EST-C015` or `EST-C014`, too loud or not finite | Feedback over 1, a filter blowing up, a division by zero | Cap feedback below 1, clamp resonance, guard divisions; smooth parameter changes. |
| `EST-C018`, two renders differ | Randomness, uninitialised state, state kept across `reset` | Seed every generator from a constant in `reset()`; reset every buffer there. |
| `EST-C017`, `EST-C028` or `EST-C006`, sound past the tail | `tail()` reports less than the plugin rings, or noise of its own | Report the real tail in frames, keep `limits.tailSeconds` (≤ 60) at least that long, cap feedback so it dies, fade self-noise out. |
| `EST-C027`, subnormal states | A feedback path or filter memory decaying forever | Set a recursive state below `1e-20` to 0. |
| `EST-C016`, no sound for a held note | An instrument's note handler or envelope is wrong | Check `noteOn` starts a voice and `render` adds it with `io.add`. |
| `EST-W009` or `EST-W010`, memory | Delay lines larger than the limit | Raise `maximumMemory` in `asconfig.json` and `limits.memoryPagesMax` in `est.json` together (64 KiB pages). |
| `EST-M002`, `EST-M003` | An id that is not reverse-DNS, a version that is not semver | `com.example.my-plugin`; `1.0.0`. |
| `EST-U002`, `EST-U005` | The window loads something from another host, or a module script | Ship every file in the bundle; one classic script (the `--app` build does it). |
| A golden test differs after a deliberate change | The reference is the old sound | `npx est test --update`. |

## Porting a VST, CLAP or JUCE plugin

Start from the `cpp-clap` template: `npx @cyber-est/cli@0.1.0 new cpp-clap my-port`. Move your DSP (plain C++, no framework types) into `src/gain.hpp` or beside it, list the sources in `est-build.json`, declare the parameters in `src/plugin.cpp`'s `kParams` and `est.json`, and run the loop. For JUCE, keep the DSP in classes that do not include JUCE headers, so the same files build for the desktop and for EST.

- Check the port against the original: render the same input through the desktop build to a WAV and run `npx est compare dist/<id>-<version>.est reference.wav --input input.wav`.
- What does not come across: a native window (make a web page window instead), threads, files, the network, `rand()` in the audio loop (seed your own generator), denormals (flush feedback paths).
- Your desktop presets become state files in `presets/` (see [Presets and levels](#presets-and-levels)).

## Adding it to Cyber and sharing it

### Put it in Cyber

In Cyber, on Home: **EST PLUGINS → Add a plugin**, and drop `dist/<id>-<version>.est` there. Cyber runs the same checks; a refusal names the same rule id. It stays on the person's own account.

Publishing on the EST Store is not part of this guide: the plugin stays on the person's own account, and they choose later what to do with it.

- **Hear it in a song**: in Cyber, put the plugin on a track (once added, the Browser lists it in Instruments, Audio Effects or MIDI Effects, after Cyber's own), play, and adjust.
- **Share it**: when the person shares the project or a listen link, the people they share with hear the plugin in that project; it plays there without being installed in their own account (a school class that keeps community plugins off hears it only in the class's own projects).
- **A new version**: raise `version` in `est.json`, run the loop, and add the new `.est` the same way; projects keep the version they were made with until the person moves them.
